# omada_session_limit (Resource)

Manages the gateway's session limiting: a cap on how many concurrent connections a single host may hold.

This is a singleton per site — import it with the site name rather than creating it.

Session limiting is a blunt instrument: a cap low enough to contain a misbehaving device will also break legitimate heavy users — a BitTorrent client or a browser opening many parallel connections can exhaust a modest limit on its own. Raise it deliberately rather than accepting a default.

~> Per-host limit rules are a separate collection in the same document and are **not** managed here; they are preserved untouched on update.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Cap on concurrent connections per host.
#
# A blunt instrument: a limit low enough to contain a misbehaving device will
# also break legitimate heavy users — a BitTorrent client or a browser opening
# many parallel connections can exhaust a modest cap by itself.
#
# Per-host rules live in the same document but are a separate collection and
# are not managed here; they are preserved on update.
resource "omada_session_limit" "this" {
  enable            = false
  max_sessions      = 128
  ip_session_enable = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `enable` (Boolean) Whether session limiting is active.
- `ip_session_enable` (Boolean) Track sessions per IP address.
- `max_sessions` (Number) Maximum concurrent sessions per host.
- `site` (String) Site name. Defaults to the primary site. Changing forces replacement.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The site ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A singleton per site — import by site name.
terraform import omada_session_limit.this Home
```
